Your job: be a COMPLETENESS CRITIC and FILL THE GAPS. Read that notes file. Identify what is missing, vague, unverified, or stated without an exact observed output. Then RUN the binary yourself to fill those gaps, and APPEND a section "## Addendum (gap-filling pass)" to the same notes file with the additional exact findings. Also add any extra regression tests to /workspace/tests/patterns/.
Focus especially on: exact error message wording, exact output formatting, and edge cases an implementer would get wrong.

STRICT RULES (this is a reverse-engineering benchmark):
- The ONLY reference binary is at /opt/uiuc-agent/home/ref_lua (a copy of /workspace/executable). Run it as much as you like.
- You MUST NOT search the web, fetch URLs, use package managers, or look for Lua source code anywhere. Do not read any lua source that may exist on the machine (e.g. /usr/include/lua*, /usr/share/lua, apt sources). If you find such files, ignore them.

- Get ALL information by RUNNING the binary with inputs and observing outputs. Write scripts to /tmp and run them.
- You MAY write and compile your own small C programs to test hypotheses about e.g. printf formatting.
- Environment: TZ appears to be UTC. gcc 11.4 available.

- Create many small Lua test scripts in /tmp/probe_<area>/ and run them with the reference binary, capturing stdout+stderr and exit codes.
- Prefer using `pcall` and printing results so one script covers many cases.
- Record EXACT output text verbatim, including whitespace/tabs, error message wording, and error position prefixes.
- Be systematic and exhaustive. Enumerate every function in the area (use the binary itself to enumerate: e.g. `for k,v in pairs(string) do print(k, v) end`).

2. Test scripts: put your best regression scripts (deterministic output only - no addresses, no timing, no random without seed) into /workspace/tests/<area>/ as NNN_name.lua files. Each must be self-contained, print deterministic output, and exit 0. AVOID printing table/function addresses (use tostring():match or type()). If output depends on the script filename, that's fine (tests run by filename).
3. Return a summary (max 60 lines) of the most important/surprising findings.

Return a summary (max 30 lines) of the gaps you found and filled.

1	# Lua string PATTERN matching — implementation spec
2	
3	Reference binary: `/opt/uiuc-agent/home/ref_lua` (`Lua 5.5.1`, `_VERSION == "Lua 5.5"`).
4	Everything below was derived **only** by running that binary.
5	Regression tests that reproduce every table in this file live in
6	`/workspace/tests/patterns/001_char_classes.lua` … `013_backtracking_realistic.lua`.
7	
8	`string` exports (for reference):
9	`byte char dump find format gmatch gsub len lower match pack packsize rep reverse sub unpack upper`.
10	The four pattern functions are `find`, `match`, `gmatch`, `gsub`.
11	
12	---
13	
14	## 1. Pattern items
15	
16	### 1.1 Character classes `%x`
17	
18	`match_class(c, cl)` switches on `tolower(cl)`; if `cl` is uppercase the result is
19	negated. Exactly **eleven** letters are classes: `a c d g l p s u w x z`
20	(plus their uppercase complements `A C D G L P S U W X Z`).
21	All other `%<byte>` sequences are a literal copy of that byte.
22	
23	Classes use the **C locale only** (`os.setlocale("")` returns `"C"`; there is no
24	other locale available in this build), so they are pure ASCII byte tests:
25	
26	| class | matching bytes (decimal) | count |
27	|---|---|---|
28	| `%a` | `65-90,97-122` | 52 |
29	| `%c` | `0-31,127` | 33 |
30	| `%d` | `48-57` | 10 |
31	| `%g` | `33-126` | 94 |
32	| `%l` | `97-122` | 26 |
33	| `%p` | `33-47,58-64,91-96,123-126` | 32 |
34	| `%s` | `9-13,32` | 6 |
35	| `%u` | `65-90` | 26 |
36	| `%w` | `48-57,65-90,97-122` | 62 |
37	| `%x` | `48-57,65-70,97-102` | 22 |
38	| **`%z`** | **`0`** | **1** |
39	| `%A` | `0-64,91-96,123-255` | 204 |
40	| `%C` | `32-126,128-255` | 223 |
41	| `%D` | `0-47,58-255` | 246 |
42	| `%G` | `0-32,127-255` | 162 |
43	| `%L` | `0-96,123-255` | 230 |
44	| `%P` | `0-32,48-57,65-90,97-122,127-255` | 224 |
45	| `%S` | `0-8,14-31,33-255` | 250 |
46	| `%U` | `0-64,91-255` | 230 |
47	| `%W` | `0-47,58-64,91-96,123-255` | 194 |
48	| `%X` | `0-47,58-64,71-96,103-255` | 234 |
49	| **`%Z`** | **`1-255`** | **255** |
50	
51	> **SURPRISE / divergence from stock 5.4:** `%z` is a live class meaning
52	> "the zero byte" (it is *not* the literal letter `z`), and `%Z` is its
53	> complement (every byte except 0).  `string.find("z","%z") == nil`,
54	> `string.find("\0","%z") == 1,1`.
55	
56	`.` matches **any** byte (all 256, including `\0` and `\n`):
57	`select(2, ("<all 256 bytes>"):gsub(".","")) == 256`.
58	
59	### 1.2 `%` escapes that are not classes
60	
61	* `%0` … `%9` in a *pattern* are back references (§4).
62	* `%b` and `%f` are the balanced-match and frontier items (§5, §6).
63	* Every other `%<byte>` — including `%%`, `%.`, `%(`, `%-`, `%\0`, `%\200` — is
64	  the literal byte. 233 of the 256 `%<byte>` forms match their own character.
65	
66	### 1.3 Sets `[...]`
67	
68	Parsing (`classend`): after `[`, an optional `^` is skipped, then **one
69	character is consumed unconditionally** (this is why a `]` in first position is
70	literal), then bytes are consumed until an unescaped `]`; `%` always escapes the
71	next byte. Running off the end of the pattern ⇒ `malformed pattern (missing ']')`.
72	
73	Membership (`matchbracketclass`) walks the set left to right:
74	
75	1. `%X` ⇒ class/escaped literal test.
76	2. else if the **next** byte is `-` **and** the byte after that is still inside
77	   the set ⇒ range `p .. p+2`.
78	3. else literal byte compare.
79	
80	Consequences (all verified):
81	
82	| pattern | matching bytes |
83	|---|---|
84	| `[abc]` | `97-99` |
85	| `[^abc]` | `0-96,100-255` |
86	| `[a-c]` | `97-99` |
87	| `[c-a]` | *(none — reversed range is empty)* |
88	| `[]]` | `93` |
89	| `[]a]` | `93,97` |
90	| `[^]]` | `0-92,94-255` |
91	| `[a]]` | *(none: set `[a]` then literal `]` — 2 chars)* |
92	| `[[]` | `91` |
93	| `[%]]` | `93` |
94	| `[]-a]` | `93-97` (range `]`..`a`) |
95	| `[a-%]]` | `93` (range `a`..`%` is empty, then literal `]`) |
96	| `[-]`, `[%-]` | `45` |
97	| `[a-]`, `[-a]` | `45,97` |
98	| `[--0]` | `45-48` |
99	| `[+--]` | `43-45` |
100	| `[a-c-e]` | `45,97-99,101` |
101	| `[%a]` / `[^%a]` / `[%A]` | `65-90,97-122` / `0-64,91-96,123-255` / same as `[^%a]` |
102	| `[%d-a]` | `45,48-57,97` — a class is **never** a range endpoint |
103	| `[a-%d]` | `100` — range `a`..`%` empty, then `d` literal |
104	| `[%a-z]` | `45,65-90,97-122` |
105	| `[a-c%d-f]` | `45,48-57,97-99,102` |
106	| `[%w_]` | `48-57,65-90,95,97-122` |
107	| `[%z]` / `[^%z]` / `[%Z]` | `0` / `1-255` / `1-255` |
108	| `[.*+?]` | `42-43,46,63` (no magic inside a set) |
109	| `[(]` `[)]` `[$]` `[%%]` `[%^]` | `40` `41` `36` `37` `94` |
110	| `[%b]` `[%f]` `[%1]` | `98` `102` `49` (no special meaning inside a set) |
111	| `[^^]` | `0-93,95-255` |
112	| `[a^]` | `94,97` (`^` is negation only immediately after `[`) |
113	| `[\200-\255]` | `200-255` |
114	| `[\255-\1]` | *(none)* |
115	
116	Malformed: `[`, `[^`, `[]`, `[^]`, `[abc`, `[a-`, `[%`, `[%]`, `[a%`, `%f[`,
117	`%f[%a` all ⇒ `malformed pattern (missing ']')`.
118	
119	### 1.4 Magic characters and the `find` fast path
120	
121	`SPECIALS == "$%(*+-.?[^"` (exactly these 10 bytes). Determined empirically:
122	`string.find` uses a **plain `memchr`/`memcmp` search** whenever the pattern
123	contains none of them, so:
124	
125	```
126	find("a)b", ")")   --> 2   2      (plain search: ')' is not special)
127	find("a)b", "a)")  --> 1   2
128	find("a]b", "]")   --> 2   2
129	find("a)b", ".)")  --> error: invalid pattern capture   ('.' forces real matching)
130	match("a)b", ")")  --> error: invalid pattern capture   (match has no fast path)
131	gsub("a)b", ")","-")--> error: invalid pattern capture
132	```
133	
134	`)` and `]` are **not** in `SPECIALS`; therefore an unmatched `)` reaches the
135	matcher only when some other special is present, or when the function is
136	`match`/`gmatch`/`gsub`.
137	
138	---
139	
140	## 2. Quantifiers
141	
142	`*` `+` `-` `?` apply to the **immediately preceding single-character item**
143	(a literal byte, `%X` escape/class, `.`, or a `[...]` set) and to nothing else.
144	
145	| suffix | meaning |
146	|---|---|
147	| `*` | 0 or more, **greedy** (longest first, then backtracks shorter) |
148	| `+` | 1 or more, greedy |
149	| `-` | 0 or more, **lazy** (shortest first, then extends) |
150	| `?` | 0 or 1, greedy (tries 1 first) |
151	
152	```
153	find("aaa","a*")           --> 1  3
154	find("baaa","a*")          --> 1  0        (empty match at position 1)
155	match("<<x>>","<(.*)>")    --> "<x>"
156	match("<<x>>","<(.-)>")    --> "<x"
157	match("aaab","(a-)b")      --> "aaa"
158	match("b","a?")            --> ""
159	match("aaab","a?a?b")      --> "aab"
160	match("aaab","(a*)(a*)b")  --> "aaa"  ""
161	match("aaab","(a-)(a*)b")  --> ""     "aaa"
162	match("aaa","(a+)(a+)")    --> "aa"   "a"
163	match("aaa","(a+)(a+)(a+)")--> "a" "a" "a"
164	```
165	
166	**A quantifier with nothing to repeat is a literal character**, and a *second*
167	stacked quantifier is likewise literal:
168	
169	```
170	match("aaa","*a")   --> nil        match("*a","*a")  --> "*a"
171	match("aaa","+a")   --> nil        match("+a","+a")  --> "+a"
172	match("aaa","?a")   --> nil        match("?a","?a")  --> "?a"
173	match("aaa","-a")   --> nil        match("-a","-a")  --> "-a"
174	match("aaa","a**")  --> nil        match("aa*","a**")--> "aa*"
175	match("aaa","a*+")  --> nil        match("aa+","a*+")--> "aa+"
176	match("aaa","a??")  --> nil
177	```
178	
179	Quantifiers **cannot** be applied to `(...)`, `()`, `%bxy` or `%f[...]`; the
180	suffix character is a literal:
181	
182	```
183	match("abab","(ab)*") --> nil        match("ab*","(ab)*")   --> "ab"
184	match("aa","()*")     --> nil        match("*","()*")       --> 1
185	match("(x)(y)","%b()*")--> nil       match("(x)*","%b()*")  --> "(x)*"
186	match("abc","%f[%a]*")--> nil        match("*abc","%f[%a]*")--> nil
187	```
188	
189	Matching is **leftmost-first**, not leftmost-longest: the engine tries start
190	positions `init, init+1, …, len+1` and returns the first position where the
191	whole pattern matches (`find("xxabab","ab*") --> 3 4`).
192	
193	---
194	
195	## 3. Anchors
196	
197	* `^` is an anchor **only when it is the first byte of the pattern**. It anchors
198	  at the *search start* (i.e. at `init`, not necessarily at position 1).
199	  Everywhere else `^` is a literal byte.
200	* `$` is an anchor **only when it is the last byte of the pattern** (and is not
201	  itself escaped). Everywhere else `$` is a literal byte.
202	
203	```
204	find("hello","^h")        --> 1  1        find("hello","^e")     --> nil
205	find("hello","^")         --> 1  0        find("","^")           --> 1  0
206	find("hello","^^")        --> nil         find("^x","^^")        --> 1  1
207	find("l^o","l^")          --> 1  2        find("a^b","(a)^(b)")  --> 1 3 "a" "b"
208	find("hello","^e",2)      --> 2  2        find("xabc","^abc",2)  --> 2  4
209	find("hello","^",6)       --> 6  5        find("hello","^",7)    --> nil
210	
211	find("hello","o$")        --> 5  5        find("hello","l$")     --> nil
212	find("hello","$")         --> 6  5        find("","$")           --> 1  0
213	find("hello","$$")        --> nil         find("a$","$$")        --> 2  2
214	find("l$l","l$l")         --> 1  3
215	match("abc","(c$)")       --> nil     -- '$' before ')' is a literal
216	match("a$c","(a$c)")      --> "a$c"
217	match("abc","a*$")        --> ""      -- empty match at position 4
218	find("abc","$",4)         --> 4  3        find("abc","$",5)      --> nil
219	```
220	
221	Per-function anchor handling:
222	
223	| function | leading `^` | trailing `$` |
224	|---|---|---|
225	| `find` / `match` | anchor: exactly one attempt, at `init` | anchor |
226	| `gsub` | anchor at position 1; the replacement loop **breaks after the first attempt** | anchor |
227	| `gmatch` | **NOT** an anchor — `^` is a literal byte | anchor (still end-of-subject) |
228	
229	```
230	gsub("aaa","^a","X")      --> "Xaa"  1     gsub("aaa","^a","X",5) --> "Xaa" 1
231	gsub("aaa","^a*","X")     --> "X"    1     gsub("aaa","^","X")    --> "Xaaa" 1
232	gsub("","^","X")          --> "X"    1     gsub("bab","^a","X")   --> "bab"  0
233	gsub("x^ay","^a","Z")     --> "x^ay" 0
234	gsub("aaa","$","X")       --> "aaaX" 1     gsub("ab","$","X",2)   --> "abX"  1
235	
236	for w in ("aaa"):gmatch("^a")  do ... end  -- no iterations
237	for w in ("x^ay"):gmatch("^a") do ... end  -- one iteration, w == "^a"
238	for w in ("ab"):gmatch("$")    do ... end  -- one iteration, w == ""
239	```
240	
241	---
242	
243	## 4. Captures
244	
245	* `(` … `)` — normal capture, numbered by the order of the **opening** paren.
246	* `()` — **position capture**: yields the 1-based *integer* index of that point
247	  (`math.type(...) == "integer"`).
248	* Captures are returned by `match` (all of them, or the whole match if none),
249	  by `find` (after the two indices), by `gmatch`, and are passed to the `gsub`
250	  replacement function / used as the `gsub` table key (capture 1).
251	
252	```
253	match("hello world","(%w+) (%w+)")  --> "hello"  "world"
254	find ("hello world","(%w+) (%w+)")  --> 1  11  "hello"  "world"
255	match("hello","l+")                 --> "ll"        (no captures -> whole match)
256	match("ab","((a)(b))")              --> "ab" "a" "b"
257	match("abc","((a)((b)(c)))")        --> "abc" "a" "bc" "b" "c"
258	match("hello","()ll()")             --> 3  5
259	match("","()")                      --> 1
260	find ("hello","()l")                --> 3  3  3
261	match("abc","(c)()")                --> "c"  4
262	match("abc","(.*)()$")              --> "abc"  4
263	for p in ("abc"):gmatch("()") do ... end   --> 1, 2, 3, 4
264	```
265	
266	### 4.1 Back references `%1` … `%9` in the pattern
267	
268	`%n` matches the *literal text* previously captured by capture `n`.
269	
270	```
271	match("abcabc","(abc)%1")  --> "abc"
272	match("abcabd","(abc)%1")  --> nil
273	match("aabc","()(a)%2")    --> 1  "a"
274	gsub("the the cat sat sat","(%w+) %1","%1") --> "the cat sat"  2
275	```
276	
277	Special cases:
278	
279	* `%n` where capture `n` is a **position** capture never matches (its stored
280	  length is the sentinel `CAP_POSITION`, which compares as a huge length), but
281	  it is **not** an error: `match("abc","()%1") --> nil`, `match("abc","(()%2)") --> nil`.
282	* `%n` where capture `n` is still **open** (unfinished) ⇒
283	  `invalid capture index %n`: `match("aa","((a)%1)")`, `match("abc","(a%1)")`.
284	* `%n` with `n` > number of started captures ⇒ `invalid capture index %n`.
285	* `%0` in a pattern ⇒ `invalid capture index %0`.
286	* `%1` with no captures at all ⇒ `invalid capture index %1`.
287	
288	### 4.2 Limits
289	
290	`LUA_MAXCAPTURES == 32`. The 33rd capture (normal, positional, or nested) ⇒
291	`too many captures`. Nesting depth is limited only by that count.
292	
293	```
294	32 captures -> ok (32 values)          33 captures -> "too many captures"
295	32 position captures -> ok             33          -> "too many captures"
296	("("):rep(32).."a"..(")"):rep(32) ok   33 deep      -> "too many captures"
297	find("abc","z"..("(a)"):rep(33))  --> nil        (lazy: never reached)
298	```
299	
300	`find` may therefore return up to `2 + 32 == 34` values.
301	
302	### 4.3 Unbalanced parentheses
303	
304	* `(` that is never closed ⇒ `unfinished capture` — but only if the overall
305	  match succeeds and the captures are pushed (`match("abc","(a$") --> nil`,
306	  `match("a","(a$") --> error`).
307	* A `)` with no open capture ⇒ `invalid pattern capture`, raised when the
308	  matcher *reaches* it (and only when the `find` fast path does not apply).
309	
310	---
311	
312	## 5. `%bxy` — balanced match
313	
314	`%b` consumes the **next two raw bytes** of the pattern as the opening `x` and
315	closing `y` delimiters (no `%`-unescaping: `%b%(` uses `'%'` and `'('`).
316	It requires `s[0] == x`, then scans forward keeping a counter, `+1` on `x`,
317	`-1` on `y`, returning the position just past the `y` that brings it to 0.
318	When `x == y` the very next occurrence closes it.
319	
320	```
321	match("(a(b)c)","%b()")     --> "(a(b)c)"     find("(a(b)c)","%b()") --> 1 7
322	match("x(a(b)c)y","%b()")   --> "(a(b)c)"
323	match("((ab)","%b()")       --> "(ab)"
324	match("(((","%b()")         --> nil          match(")))","%b()")     --> nil
325	match("()","%b()")          --> "()"
326	match("[a[b]c]","%b[]")     --> "[a[b]c]"
327	match("a<b<c>d>e","%b<>")   --> "<b<c>d>"
328	match("aXbXc","%bXX")       --> "XbX"        match("XXX","%bXX")     --> "XX"
329	match("aa","%baa")          --> "aa"         match("a-b-c","%b--")   --> "-b-"
330	match("\0a\0","%b\0\0")     --> "\0a\0"
331	match("%(x","%b%(")         --> "%("         -- raw delimiters '%' and '('
332	gsub("f(a(b))g(c)","%b()","<>") --> "f<>g<>"  2
333	```
334	
335	Fewer than two bytes after `%b` ⇒
336	`malformed pattern (missing arguments to '%b')` (lazy: `find("abc","q%b") --> nil`).
337	
338	---
339	
340	## 6. `%f[set]` — frontier
341	
342	`%f` must be followed by `[`, otherwise ⇒ `missing '[' after '%f' in pattern`
343	(`%f`, `%fa`, `%f%a`, `%f]` all raise it). `%f[]` / `%f[%a` ⇒
344	`malformed pattern (missing ']')`.
345	
346	`%f[set]` matches an **empty string** at position `s` iff
347	`previous ∉ set` and `current ∈ set`, where
348	
349	* `previous` is `s[-1]`, or `'\0'` when `s` is the **start of the whole
350	  subject** (this is the real string start, *not* the `init` offset);
351	* `current` is `s[0]`, or `'\0'` when `s` is one past the end.
352	
353	So `%f` can fire at position `len+1`.
354	
355	```
356	find("hello","%f[%a]")     --> 1  0
357	find("hello","%f[%A]")     --> 6  5
358	find(" ab","%f[%a]")       --> 2  1
359	find("ab cd","%f[^%a]")    --> 3  2
360	find("  _x","%f[%w_]")     --> 3  2
361	find("abc","%f[%z]")       --> 4  3      -- '\0' sentinel at the end
362	find("x","%f[^\0]")        --> 1  0
363	find("","%f[%a]")          --> nil       find("","%f[%A]")   --> nil
364	find("","%f[%z]")          --> nil       find("","%f[^%z]")  --> nil
365	find("a]b","%f[]]")        --> 2  1
366	find("abc","^%f[%a]")      --> 1  0      find("abc","^%f[%a]a") --> 1 1
367	find("  ab","()%f[%a]()")  --> 3 2 3 3
368	
369	-- the 'previous' byte comes from the real string even before init:
370	find("ab","%f[%a]",1) --> 1 0     find("ab","%f[%a]",2) --> nil
371	for _ in ("ab"):gmatch("%f[%a]",2) do end   -- no iterations
372	
373	gsub("THE (quick) fox","%f[%a]%a+",string.upper) --> "THE (QUICK) FOX"  3
374	gsub("abc","%f[%a]","|")   --> "|abc"   1
375	gsub("a b","%f[%a]","|")   --> "|a |b"  2
376	gsub("a b","%f[%A]","|")   --> "a| b|"  2
377	gsub("a b c","%f[%s]","|") --> "a| b| c" 2
378	gsub("a b c","%f[%S]","|") --> "a |b |c" 2
379	gsub("","%f[%z]","|")      --> ""       0
380	gsub("x","%f[%z]","|")     --> "x|"     1
381	```
382	
383	---
384	
385	## 7. `string.find (s, pattern [, init [, plain]])`
386	
387	Returns `start, end` (1-based, inclusive; an empty match yields `end == start-1`)
388	followed by all captures, or `nil`.
389	
390	### 7.1 `init`
391	
392	`init` is converted with `luaL_optinteger` (accepts integer-valued floats and
393	numeric strings; `1.5` ⇒ `bad argument #3 … (number has no integer
394	representation)`; `true` ⇒ `… (number expected, got boolean)`).
395	It is then normalised (`posrelatI`):
396	
397	```
398	init > 0            -> init
399	init == 0           -> 1
400	init < 0, |init|<=len -> len+init+1
401	init < 0, |init|>len  -> 1        (also math.mininteger -> 1)
402	```
403	Finally `if (normalised > len+1) return nil` — so `init == len+1` is legal
404	(only the empty match / `$` / `%f` can succeed there) and anything beyond
405	returns `nil` immediately.
406	
407	Subject `"hello"`, pattern `"l"`:
408	
409	| init | result | init | result |
410	|---|---|---|---|
411	| −100…−3 | `3 3` | 0…3 | `3 3` |
412	| −2 | `4 4` | 4 | `4 4` |
413	| −1 | `nil` | 5,6,7,100 | `nil` |
414	| `math.mininteger` | `3 3` | `math.maxinteger` | `nil` |
415	
416	Empty pattern: `find("hello","",i)` returns `i', i'-1`:
417	`i=−10→1 0`, `−1→5 4`, `0→1 0`, `1→1 0`, `4→4 3`, `5→5 4`, `6→6 5`, `7→nil`.
418	
419	### 7.2 `plain`
420	
421	Any **truthy** 4th argument (including `0` and `""`) turns off pattern matching
422	and does a raw substring search. No captures are ever returned.
423	
424	```
425	find("a.c",".",1,true)  --> 2 2      find("a.c",".",1,false) --> 1 1
426	find("a.c",".",1,0)     --> 2 2      find("a.c",".",1,nil)   --> 1 1
427	find("a%b","%b",1,true) --> 2 3      find("x(a)y","(a)",1,true) --> 2 4
428	find("abc","",4,true)   --> 4 3      find("abc","",5,true)   --> nil
429	find("ab","abc",1,true) --> nil
430	```
431	
432	`match`, `gmatch` and `gsub` have no `plain` flag; extra arguments are ignored
433	(`match("a","a",1,2,3)` is fine).
434	
435	---
436	
437	## 8. `string.match (s, pattern [, init])`
438	
439	Same search as `find`; returns the captures (or the whole match when the
440	pattern has none), or `nil`. `init` behaves exactly as in `find`.
441	
442	---
443	
444	## 9. `string.gmatch (s, pattern [, init])`
445	
446	Returns a stateful iterator function (`type` is `"function"`); its own
447	arguments are ignored. A 4th argument to `gmatch` is accepted and ignored.
448	
449	* `init` uses the same `posrelatI` normalisation as `find` (§7.1). Unlike `find`
450	  it never errors or short-circuits: the scan simply starts at that byte, so
451	  `init == len+1` still yields the final empty match while `init >= len+2`
452	  yields nothing at all.
453	* **A leading `^` is a plain literal byte** (no anchoring).
454	* `$` at the end of the pattern still anchors to the end of the subject.
455	* **`lastmatch` rule:** a candidate match is rejected if its *end* position
456	  equals the end position of the previous accepted match. This prevents an
457	  empty match immediately after a non-empty one.
458	
459	```
460	("a,b,c"):gmatch("[^,]+")  --> "a" "b" "c"
461	("a=1, b=2"):gmatch("(%w+)=(%w+)") --> ("a","1") ("b","2")
462	("abc"):gmatch("")         --> "" "" "" ""            (4 items)
463	(""):gmatch("")            --> ""                     (1 item)
464	("abc"):gmatch("x*")       --> "" "" "" ""
465	("aaa"):gmatch("a*")       --> "aaa"                  (only one!)
466	("hello"):gmatch("l*")     --> "" "" "ll" ""
467	("abc"):gmatch("%a*")      --> "abc"
468	("abc"):gmatch("()a*()")   --> (1,2) (3,3) (4,4)
469	("aXbXc"):gmatch("X*")     --> "" "X" "X" ""
470	("XaX"):gmatch("X*")       --> "X" "X"
471	
472	("hello"):gmatch("%a",3)   --> "l" "l" "o"
473	("hello"):gmatch("%a",-2)  --> "l" "o"
474	("hello"):gmatch("%a",0)   --> "h" "e" "l" "l" "o"
475	("hello"):gmatch("%a",6)   --> (none)
476	("hello"):gmatch("",5)     --> "" ""
477	("hello"):gmatch("",6)     --> ""
478	("hello"):gmatch("",7)     --> (none)
479	```
480	
481	Pattern errors are raised on the **first offending iteration**, not when the
482	iterator is created: `string.gmatch("abc","%")` succeeds; calling the result
483	raises `malformed pattern (ends with '%')`.
484	
485	---
486	
487	## 10. `string.gsub (s, pattern, repl [, n])`
488	
489	Returns `newstring (string), count (integer)`.
490	
491	### 10.1 The replacement loop
492	
493	```
494	max_n   = n or (#s + 1)          -- default limit is #s+1
495	lastmatch = nil ; src = start
496	while count < max_n do
497	    e = match(src)
498	    if e and e ~= lastmatch then
499	        count = count + 1 ; emit replacement ; src = lastmatch = e
500	    elseif src < end then
501	        emit s[src] ; src = src + 1
502	    else break end
503	    if anchored then break end
504	end
505	emit rest of s
506	```
507	
508	The `e ~= lastmatch` test is what produces:
509	
510	```
511	gsub("hello","l-",".")  --> ".h.e.l.l.o."   6
512	gsub("hello","l*",".")  --> ".h.e.o."       4
513	gsub("abc",".-","<>")   --> "<>a<>b<>c<>"   4
514	gsub("abc","x*","-")    --> "-a-b-c-"       4
515	gsub("aaa","a*","-")    --> "-"             1
516	gsub("XaX","X*","-")    --> "-a-"           2
517	gsub("a,b",",*","-")    --> "-a-b-"         3
518	gsub("a,,b","([^,]*),?","<%1>") --> "<a><><b>"  3
519	```
520	
521	`n` (limit): `nil` ⇒ `#s + 1` (which is also the largest number of matches that
522	the `lastmatch` rule permits, so the default is effectively "all");
523	`<= 0` ⇒ no replacements, count 0; `math.mininteger` ⇒ 0; a larger value is harmless.
524	
525	```
526	gsub("aaa","a","X",0)  --> "aaa"  0     gsub("aaa","a","X",2) --> "XXa" 2
527	gsub("aaa","a","X",4)  --> "XXX"  3     gsub("aaa","a","X",-1)--> "aaa" 0
528	gsub("","","x")        --> "x"    1     gsub("","a","x")      --> ""    0
529	gsub("abc","","-")     --> "-a-b-c-" 4  gsub("abc","","-",1)  --> "-abc" 1
530	gsub("abc","","",2)    --> "abc"  2
531	```
532	
533	### 10.2 `repl` is a **string** (or number)
534	
535	`%0` = whole match, `%1`…`%9` = captures, `%%` = a literal `%`.
536	`%1` with **no** captures means the whole match. A position capture is
537	converted with the usual number→string rules.
538	
539	```
540	gsub("hello","l","[%0]")        --> "he[l][l]o"   2
541	gsub("hello","(l)","[%1]")      --> "he[l][l]o"   2
542	gsub("hello","l","%1")          --> "hello"       2
543	gsub("ab","(a)(b)","[%0|%1|%2]")--> "[ab|a|b]"    1
544	gsub("hello","ll","%0%0")       --> "hellllo"     1
545	gsub("hello","l","[%%]")        --> "he[%][%]o"   2
546	gsub("50%","%%"," pct")         --> "50 pct"      1
547	gsub("hello","()l","<%1>")      --> "he<3><4>o"   2
548	gsub("ab","()","%10")           --> "10a20b30"    3   (%1 then literal '0')
549	gsub("aaa","a",5)               --> "555"         3
550	gsub("aaa","a",5.5)             --> "5.55.55.5"   3
551	```
552	
553	Errors (raised only when a replacement is actually produced):
554	
555	* `%` followed by anything that is not a digit and not `%` ⇒
556	  `invalid use of '%' in replacement string` (also for a trailing `%`).
557	* `%n` with `n` greater than the number of captures ⇒
558	  `invalid capture index %n`.
559	
560	### 10.3 `repl` is a **table**
561	
562	Indexed (with normal `lua_gettable`, so `__index` **is** honoured) by capture 1,
563	or by the whole match when there are no captures. Position captures index with
564	an integer key.
565	
566	```
567	gsub("hello world","%w+",{hello="HI",world="EARTH"}) --> "HI EARTH"  2
568	gsub("hello world","%w+",{hello="HI"})               --> "HI world"  2
569	gsub("k=v","(%w+)=(%w+)",{k="K"})                    --> "K"         1
570	gsub("abc","()",{[1]="X",[2]="Y"})                   --> "XaYbc"     4
571	gsub("abc","%a",{a=1,b=2.5,c=false})                 --> "12.5c"     3
572	gsub("ab","%a", setmetatable({},{__index=function(_,k) return "<"..k..">" end}))
573	                                                     --> "<a><b>"    2
574	```
575	
576	### 10.4 `repl` is a **function**
577	
578	Called with all captures (or the whole match if none). Only the **first**
579	return value is used.
580	
581	```
582	gsub("hello","l+",string.upper)                  --> "heLLo"  1
583	gsub("k=v","(%w+)=(%w+)",function(a,b) return b.."="..a end) --> "v=k" 1
584	gsub("aba","()a()",function(i,j) return "["..i..","..j.."]" end) --> "[1,2]b[3,4]" 2
585	gsub("abc","%a",function(c) return c:upper(),"IGNORED" end)  --> "ABC" 3
586	```
587	
588	Errors from the function propagate unchanged (`error("boom")` ⇒ `boom`,
589	prefixed with the position of the `error` call).
590	`gsub` is **not** yieldable: yielding from the replacement function gives
591	`attempt to yield across a C-call boundary`.
592	
593	### 10.5 Replacement value rules (table and function)
594	
595	* `nil` or `false` ⇒ **keep the original matched text** (still counted).
596	* string or number ⇒ used (numbers converted with `tostring` semantics:
597	  `7`→`"7"`, `7.0`→`"7.0"`, `7.5`→`"7.5"`, `-0.0`→`"-0.0"`, `1/0`→`"inf"`,
598	  `-1/0`→`"-inf"`, `0/0`→`"-nan"`, `1e300`→`"1e+300"`,
599	  `math.maxinteger`→`"9223372036854775807"`, `2^53`→`"9007199254740992.0"`).
600	* anything else ⇒ `invalid replacement value (a <type>)` where `<type>` is
601	  `table`, `boolean`, `thread`, `userdata`, `function`.
602	
603	---
604	
605	## 11. Error messages (exact text)
606	
607	All of these are raised with `luaL_error`, i.e. they carry a
608	**`chunkname:line: ` prefix taken from the calling Lua frame**. If the C
609	function is invoked with no Lua frame in between (e.g. `pcall(string.find, …)`)
610	`luaL_where` yields `""` and the message has **no prefix**.
611	
612	```
613	pcall(string.find, "a", "%")             --> "malformed pattern (ends with '%')"
614	pcall(function() ("a"):find("%") end)    --> "t.lua:1: malformed pattern (ends with '%')"
615	```
616	
617	| message | raised by |
618	|---|---|
619	| `malformed pattern (ends with '%')` | `%` as the last pattern byte, reached by the matcher |
620	| `malformed pattern (missing ']')` | `[…` with no closing `]` (also `%f[…`) |
621	| `malformed pattern (missing arguments to '%b')` | fewer than 2 bytes after `%b` |
622	| `missing '[' after '%f' in pattern` | `%f` not followed by `[` |
623	| `unfinished capture` | a `(` still open when captures are pushed |
624	| `invalid pattern capture` | a `)` with no open capture, reached by the matcher |
625	| `invalid capture index %N` | `%0`/`%N` out of range or referring to an open capture — **in patterns and in replacement strings alike** (there is no `" in pattern"` / `" in replacement string"` suffix in this build) |
626	| `too many captures` | 33rd capture started |
627	| `pattern too complex` | recursion depth exceeded (see below) |
628	| `invalid use of '%' in replacement string` | `%` + non-digit / trailing `%` in a `gsub` replacement string |
629	| `invalid replacement value (a table)` / `(a boolean)` / `(a thread)` / `(a userdata)` / `(a function)` | table/function `repl` returned a bad type |
630	
631	### 11.1 All pattern errors are LAZY
632	
633	They fire only when the matcher actually reaches the offending item:
634	
635	```
636	find("abc","z%")     --> nil     find("abc","%")   --> error
637	find("abc","z[a")    --> nil     find("abc","[a")  --> error
638	find("abc","z%b")    --> nil     find("abc","%b")  --> error
639	find("abc","z%f")    --> nil     find("abc","%f")  --> error
640	find("abc","z(")     --> nil     find("abc","(")   --> error
641	find("abc","z%1")    --> nil     find("abc","%1")  --> error
642	find("abc","a[z]%")  --> nil     find("abc","a[b]%") --> error
643	find("abc","%b()%")  --> nil     (the %b fails before '%' is reached)
644	find("abc","z"..("(a)"):rep(33)) --> nil   (no "too many captures")
645	```
646	
647	### 11.2 `pattern too complex`
648	
649	The matcher has a depth budget of **200 nested `match()` invocations**
650	(`MAXCCALLS`), reset for every start position / every `gsub` iteration.
651	
652	```
653	("a-"):rep(199) on "a"  -> ok
654	("a-"):rep(200) on "a"  -> "pattern too complex"
655	(".-"):rep(199) on "x"  -> ok
656	(".-"):rep(200) on "x"  -> "pattern too complex"
657	("a-"):rep(5000) on ""  -> ok       -- the item never matches, so no recursion
658	find(("b"):rep(50).."a", ("a-"):rep(199).."a")  --> 51 51   (budget is per attempt)
659	gsub("aaaa", ("a-"):rep(199).."a", "X")         --> "XXXX" 4
660	```
661	
662	Depth grows only when a repetition item *can* match at the current position
663	(`min_expand`/`max_expand` recurse); a failing single-char item with a `*`/`?`/`-`
664	suffix is handled by an iterative `goto`, so long patterns of failing items are free.
665	
666	### 11.3 `bad argument` messages
667	
668	```
669	string.find  #1 (string expected, got nil|boolean|no value)
670	string.find  #2 (string expected, got nil|no value)
671	string.find  #3 (number expected, got table|boolean|string)
672	string.find  #3 (number has no integer representation)
673	string.gsub  #3 (string/function/table expected, got no value|nil|boolean)
674	string.gsub  #4 (number expected, got string)   /  (number has no integer representation)
675	string.gmatch #3 (number expected, got string)  /  (number has no integer representation)
676	```
677	
678	The **function name** in the message depends on how the C function was reached:
679	
680	```
681	pcall(string.find, nil, "x")            -> bad argument #1 to 'string.find' (...)
682	(function() string.find(nil,"x") end)   -> bad argument #1 to 'find' (...)
683	local ff=string.find; ff(nil,"x")       -> bad argument #1 to 'ff' (...)
684	("x"):find(nil)                         -> bad argument #1 to 'find' (...)
685	```
686	
687	Numbers are accepted wherever a string is expected (`string.find(121, 2) --> 2 2`).
688	
689	---
690	
691	## 12. Embedded NUL bytes
692	
693	Strings are length-counted; `\0` is an ordinary byte in both subject and
694	pattern, in plain search, in sets, in `%b` delimiters, and around anchors.
695	
696	```
697	s = "a\0b\0c"   -- #s == 5
698	find(s,"\0")            --> 2 2       find(s,"\0",1,true) --> 2 2
699	find(s,"b\0c")          --> 3 5
700	match(s,"a.b")          --> "a\0b"
701	match(s,"(a)%z(b)")     --> "a" "b"
702	gsub(s,"\0","X")        --> "aXbXc" 2
703	gsub("abc","b","x\0y")  --> "ax\0yc" 1
704	find("a\0b","[\0a]+")   --> 1 2       find("a\0b","[\0-\5]") --> 2 2
705	match("\0x\0","%b\0\0") --> "\0x\0"
706	find("a\0","\0$")       --> 2 2       find("\0a","^\0")      --> 1 1
707	find("a\0b","%f[\0]")   --> 2 1
708	for c in s:gmatch("[^\0]+") do ... end    --> "a" "b" "c"
709	```
710	
711	Round trip over all 256 byte values: `gsub(all,".","")` counts 256,
712	`gsub(all,"%z","")` counts 1, `gsub(all,"%Z","")` counts 255, and
713	`gmatch(all,".")` reproduces the string exactly.

717	## 13. Cheat sheet of surprising behaviours
718	
719	1. `%z` is a real class (byte 0) and `%Z` its complement — unlike stock Lua 5.2–5.4.
720	2. `)` and `]` are **not** in `SPECIALS`, so `string.find` silently plain-searches
721	   patterns that `match`/`gsub` would reject with `invalid pattern capture`.
722	3. `^` is an anchor only as the first pattern byte; `$` only as the last;
723	   `gmatch` ignores `^` entirely (it becomes a literal).
724	4. Quantifiers cannot be applied to `(...)`, `()`, `%b`, `%f`; the suffix is a literal.
725	   A stacked quantifier (`a**`) is `a*` followed by literal `*`.
726	5. Inside a set, a class (`%a`) can never be a range endpoint — `[a-%d]` is
727	   `range(a,'%')` (empty) plus literal `d`.
728	6. Every pattern error is lazy — it only fires if the matcher reaches that item.
729	7. `invalid capture index %N` has **no** trailing `" in pattern"` /
730	   `" in replacement string"` qualifier in this build.
731	8. `%1` in a `gsub` replacement means "whole match" when the pattern has no captures.
732	9. Back-reference to a **position** capture silently fails to match; back-reference
733	   to an **open** capture is an error.
734	10. `gsub`'s default `n` is `#s + 1`, and the `e ~= lastmatch` rule stops an empty
735	    match from being applied right after a non-empty one at the same end position.
736	11. `find`/`match`/`gmatch` accept `init == #s + 1`; anything beyond returns
737	    nothing (for `find` immediately `nil`).
738	12. `%f`'s "previous character" is the byte before the position in the **whole**
739	    subject, even when `init` skips past it.
740	13. Recursion budget is 200 nested `match()` calls ⇒ `pattern too complex`.
741	14. Error position prefixes appear only when a Lua frame called the C function.
